{'index': 0, 'translation': 'Looking at some of the comments here, you’ll find a vocal group publicly opposing every AI tool, including Apple Intelligence. They may be a minority, but their voices are particularly loud. This situation has given rise to an unofficial tool that lets users disable this feature on Mac and delete all downloaded Siri AI models.'}

{'index': 1, 'translation': 'We mentioned yesterday that doing so could come with risks, but some are now pointing out that Apple, in order to protect hardware sales, may ultimately have to officially support the ability to remove AI…'}

{'index': 2, 'translation': 'In recent years, opposition to generative AI has continued to grow in society, with opponents citing a wide range of reasons — from concerns about the survival of the human species to simply not wanting their devices’ storage taken up by unwanted AI.'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': 'The latest Apple Intelligence models require up to 14GB of storage space, which is a significant impact for users of 256GB devices who don’t want these features. This is why independent developer Om Lahore created the tool RemoveMacAI.'}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'Posted by GoldGrapes'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': 'Setting aside the "minority but loud" point, are you also trying to say that their actions will threaten hardware sales, so Apple must support a system-level AI removal feature? How could a minority group possibly affect sales figures?'}

{'index': 6, 'translation': 'As we warned yesterday, using this tool is not without risks. Since Apple Intelligence is deeply embedded in macOS 27, it may cause unforeseen impacts on some basic functions.'}

{'index': 7, 'translation': 'However, some believe Apple may ultimately have to provide an official method for users to remove Apple Intelligence on Mac. John Gruber of Daring Fireball specifically pointed out that some organizations have already banned the installation of AI tools.'}

{'index': 8, 'translation': 'To be clear, Apple already offers quite a few management options for organizations using device management. Apple says organizations can "restrict the use" of certain Apple Intelligence features, and there are individual toggles to switch each feature on or off separately. What’s currently missing is a master switch that can disable all Apple Intelligence features at once, and an option to completely delete the downloaded models.'}

{'index': 9, 'translation': 'This issue is not yet urgent, but when future Macs begin to drop support for older versions of macOS, if AI models still cannot be easily removed, it could well start to affect Apple’s hardware sales.'}
